resolutions.finding: The 18-month figure is the current controlling one. Rule 61C-1.002, F.A.C. (Licensing and Inspection Requirements) requires plan review for a public food service establishment 'reopened after being out of business for more than 18 months,' and provides that plan review is not required for change-of-ownership applications 'when no interruption in operation or no change to the establishment occurs.' DBPR's current application packet (Form HR-7030, May 2024, incorporated by reference into Rule 61C-1.002) states the same test: plan review is required when an establishment is 're-opened after being closed at least 18 months,' and 'Applications for change of ownership do not require a plan review if no interruption in operation, construction or remodeling occurs.' The competing 'closed at least 1 year' / 'less than a year' language came from older DBPR form versions (the HR-7007-era packet) and an older version of the rule (a 2011 rulemaking notice shows the 12-month text being amended); it is superseded. So: change of ownership with no interruption/remodel = no plan review; reopening after 18+ months closed = plan review required.
resolutions.question: (a) DBPR change-of-ownership timing

resolutions.finding: Filing-frequency tiers (s. 212.11(1)(c), F.S., as implemented by DOR): MONTHLY if the dealer paid more than $1,000 in sales and use tax during the most recent state fiscal year (July 1-June 30); QUARTERLY if the tax remitted for the preceding four calendar quarters did not exceed $1,000 ('$1,000 (the maximum amount allowed for quarterly filing)' per DOR TIP 02A01-17, opened at https://FloridaRevenue.com/taxes/tips/documents/TIP_02A01-17.pdf); SEMIANNUAL if the dealer paid less than $500 in sales and use tax during four consecutive quarters (DOR TIP 98A01-02, opened at https://FLORIDAREVENUE.COM/taxes/tips/documents/TIP_98A01-02.pdf); ANNUAL if the tax remitted for the preceding four calendar quarters did not exceed $100 (s. 212.11(1)(c)3, F.S. - the controlling statute cited by the DOR materials; no current freestanding DOR page restating the $100 annual tier was located, the DR-15N instructions do not include the tier table). Mandatory electronic filing: taxpayers who paid $5,000 or more in sales and use tax during the prior state fiscal year 'are required to file returns and pay tax electronically during the next calendar year,' and consolidated filers must e-file regardless of amount (DOR Instructions for DR-15, Form DR-15N, R. 10/25, eff. 12/25). Note: older DOR TIPs (2003-2007, e.g. TIP 03A01-09 at https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/tips/documents/TIP_03A01-09.pdf) cited a $30,000 e-file threshold; the current DR-15N instructions state $5,000, so $5,000 is the current figure and the $30,000 figure is outdated.
resolutions.question: (b) DOR sales-tax filing-frequency tiers

resolutions.finding: No published dollar fee for any of the three items was located on official Miami-Dade County pages. What was established: (1) the Local Business Tax schedule lives in County Code Sec. 8A-223.1 (confirmed in the county's own 11/15/2022 agenda backup, miamidade.gov); the restaurant-classification fee itself is not published in a citable county page found; (2) no Certificate of Use fee schedule for restaurants was found on county pages; (3) the county's 'Find a Permit' page references a 'Fire Prevention Fee Schedule' Implementing Order covering fire life-safety inspection fees, but the dollar schedule was not retrieved. On the reported Sept 2026 Ch. 14 ordinance: NOT confirmed from any official county source. Third-party reports (realtor.com AI-generated local news, Aug-Sep 2026) say the BCC approved an ordinance sponsored by Commissioner Roberto J. Gonzalez moving small-business fire inspections from annual to every two years (biennial operating permits for business occupancies of 1,500 sq ft or less), applicable countywide. However, the county's official Life Safety Operating Permit page (opened) still states 'all businesses are required to have an annual inspection and receive a Life Safety Operating Permit,' and no county press release, clerk's legislative record, or ordinance text for the 2026 Ch. 14 change was located.
resolutions.follow_up: A human should pull the 2026 Board of County Commissioners legislative record (County Clerk govaction/legistar) for the Chapter 14 fire-prevention ordinance sponsored by Commissioner Gonzalez - confirm ordinance number, adoption date, and effective date - and re-check the Fire Rescue Life Safety permit page for updates. For fees: request the current Sec. 8A-223.1 schedule of taxes (LBTR), the RER Certificate of Use fee schedule, and the Fire Prevention Fee Schedule Implementing Order from the county (Tax Collector: 305-270-4949; Fire Prevention: 786-331-4800).
resolutions.question: (c) Miami-Dade fee schedules

resolutions.finding: Confirmed from the Florida Department of Revenue's official Property Taxpayers - Tangible Personal Property page (floridarevenue.com): 'Failure to file will result in a penalty of 25 percent of the total tax levied against the property for each year that you do not file a return. Filing late will result in a penalty of 5 percent of the total tax levied against the property covered by that return for each year, each month, and part of a month that a return is late, but not more than 25 percent of the total tax. Failure to list all TPP on the return will result in a penalty of 15 percent of the tax attributable to the omitted property.' This matches s. 193.072(1)(a)-(c), F.S. (25% failure to file; 5%/month late filing capped at 25%; 15% unlisted property), so the round-1 figures are corroborated by an official state (DOR) source. (Direct fetches of the s. 193.072 text on flsenate.gov timed out from this environment, as in round 1.)
resolutions.question: (d) TPP late/non-filing penalties
